project.title: JennieJoy Kids — A Day at the Zoo

audience: Children under three, especially two-year-old English learners; gentle unhurried language and repeat pauses.
style: Original high-quality preschool 2D character animation, clean warm-dark-brown outlines, soft hand-painted storybook backgrounds, restrained pastel palette of rose pink, dusty teal, sage, warm cream and pale sky blue, moderate contrast and soft warm daylight. Keep Alice's pink recognizable but less glaring than the reference; no fluorescent or aggressively saturated colors. Rounded friendly animal anatomy, readable silhouettes, purposeful hand-drawn acting, natural anticipation, overlapping hair and cloth movement, grounded alternating walk cycles, independent elbow and knee bends, gaze changes and blinks. No photo collage, floating cutouts, static poster zoom, realistic skin, glossy plastic 3D, or copied TV-series characters. 1920x1080 delivery, 16:9 composition, 24 fps editorial timeline. Reserve the lower 18 percent as quiet subtitle-safe background without hiding shoes; keep every face above that zone.
purpose: Learn and repeat English zoo vocabulary through a gentle family story.

image_style_library.adaptation: Adapt identity and scene composition guidance to restrained preschool cartoon artwork, with no corporate photorealism or unprovided logos.

scenes.setting: A welcoming cream-and-sage zoo gate beside rounded trees and a warm stone path. No readable text is generated on the gate.
scenes.lighting: Soft warm daylight, diffuse shadows, restrained pastel storybook palette; no oversaturation.
scenes.camera: Medium-wide eye-level family shot; gentle rightward tracking with the walking family, no sudden zoom.
scenes.action: 0.000–1.200 seconds: Start already in a friendly living pose. Alice holds Mother's right hand with her left hand and Father's left hand with her right hand. The family takes two small grounded steps toward the zoo entrance. 1.200–3.153 seconds: Alice looks from Mother to Father, then toward the audience, smiling as the first line is spoken. Parents exchange a fond silent glance. 3.153–4.000 seconds: The family stops with planted feet. Parents gently release Alice's hands. 4.000–6.073 seconds: Alice points toward the gate with her right index finger, leans forward with delight and speaks the second line. Both parents follow her gaze. 6.073–9.700 seconds: Alice returns her hand to a relaxed pose, mouth resting. Hold a welcoming repeat-after-me pause with one natural blink and subtle breathing. 9.700–10.000 seconds: The family starts a slow step forward; a nearby leafy branch softly crosses the lens to motivate the next scene.
scenes.music: Gentle low-volume instrumental, sparse ukulele and bells; no lyrics, duck under speech.
